content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +10–20% in true values), model forecasts overshoot initially but then fall too quickly, failing to sustain the peak.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate and correct for prolonged upward trends in true values.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in high-variance periods (e.g., 2023-01-23–25), underestimating both magnitude and duration of rallies.
- Model exhibits “early correction” bias — overreacts to recent price drops, leading to premature downward revisions.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are systematically too low, especially when true values show strong upward momentum in the first 10–15 days.
